title: ManyChat Pricing 2026: Plans and Contact Tier Costs
summary: ManyChat pricing is based on contact count, not the displayed plan price. Calculate what you'll actually pay based on your messaging volume.
body_markdown:
## Hidden ManyChat costs and limits people hit


After the upgrade, five costs catch ManyChat buyers: contact tier jumps, channel provider fees, AI usage limits, features limited to Pro, and Meta's messaging rules. Each one comes with a check you can run before you pay.


- Tier jumps: look at your contact count and growth over the next three months.
- Channel fees: price your WhatsApp or SMS volume with the provider, not with ManyChat.
- AI limits: read the usage allowance for your plan before building around AI replies.
- Pro-locked features: list the integrations and API calls your setup needs.
- Meta rules: check how often you message people outside the reply window.


### Contact-based tier jumps


Because your bill follows your contact list, not your activity, a list that grows quietly can push you up a tier.


Past your plan's included contacts,[ManyChat](https://manychat.com/pricing) charges $0.10 per extra contact on Essential. That means 1,000 extra contacts add $100. Pro charges $0.05, so the same 1,000 add $50.


Business charges $0.025, and Advanced charges $0.004, which means Advanced costs roughly one-sixth as much.


Check this before upgrading: if you're regularly adding contacts, a higher plan can cost less per head than overage on a lower one.


A cheap plan with heavy WhatsApp traffic can cost far more than the plan price suggests, because outside providers carry WhatsApp and SMS and bill you separately for the messages. The ManyChat subscription pays for the tool, not the delivery.


Check this before upgrading: estimate your monthly message volume and price it with the provider first.


### ManyChat features that require the Pro plan


Most often, integrations and API access force a Pro upgrade. If your setup sends data to a CRM or a spreadsheet, you may find out on Essential that the connection isn't available.


If the only job is getting a lead into a CRM, a sheet or a helpdesk,[Activepieces](https://www.activepieces.com/) can take that handoff alongside ManyChat, not in place of it.


Its pricing page bills 1 credit per flow run, whether the run has two steps or ten, so splitting the handoff into small, separate steps (CRM record, sheet row, helpdesk ticket) costs the same as cramming it into one.


Zapier's per-task billing and Make's per-module billing charge for each of those steps. The free plan is $0 with 1,000 credits a month and unlimited flows.


A flow that leans on AI replies can hit a ceiling mid-month, because usage limits cap the AI features.


Check this before upgrading: write down every outside tool your flow touches, then confirm each one is included on the plan you're buying.


### Meta messaging rules that limit ManyChat sends


Meta, which owns Instagram, Messenger and WhatsApp, restricts when you can message someone. For most conversations you can reply freely for a limited window after the person last wrote to you. Outside it, you're limited to approved message types.


No ManyChat plan removes that rule, so paying more won't buy back reach you never had.


Check this before upgrading: look at how many of your planned messages go to people who haven't written to you recently. If the answer is most of them, fix the plan for that audience before you pick a tier.
